recipes.name: Sweet, Sticky, and Spicy Chicken
ingredients_raw: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into 1/2 inch strips

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, honey, hot sauce, brown sugar, ginger, and garlic together in a small bowl; set sauce aside.
Lightly season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chicken; cook and stir until browned, about 1 minute per side.
Pour sauce over chicken; simmer, uncovered, until sauce thickens, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet, Sticky, and Spicy Chicken
raw_recipe.description: A sticky chicken recipe featuring a blend of sweet, spicy, and savory flavors thanks to the addition of honey, ginger, soy, and hot sauce.

video.description: Strips of chicken breast simmer in a sweet, spicy, gingery sauce.

review.reviewBody: Sweet...yes. Spicy...yes. Sticky...no Very good flavor but I had the same problem other reviewers mentioned about the sauce not thickening up. I will make it again with the following changes: 1. Dredging the chicken strips in flour before sauteing, which will help them brown better and help thicken the sauce. 2. Saute on med.-high heat instead of medium. The heat called for in the recipe is not enough to sear the chicken. 3. Simmer the sauce while I am preparing the chicken, then add to the chicken as called for. Because, it took much longer than 8-10 minutes to reduce the sauce, and the chicken dried out. I should add my husband loved this recipe. The flavors are good. Thanks.

I followed the recipe pretty much exactly. I did notice that when I poured the sauce over the chicken, it seemed to be taking way too long to reduce. I was also afraid of over-cooking the chicken, so I took it out of the pan. When the sauce reduced to a thick molasses constistancy, I put the chicken back in to coat it. I think the juices of the chicken were keeping the sauce from reducing properly and I wanted the chicken juice in the chicken, not the sauce. This came out good and we enjoyed it, but the chicken was a trifle dry. Next time I'll remove the chicken as soon as it's browned, reduce the sauce and then add the chicken back. Thanks for the recipe!

A-MA-ZING...simply amazing! I followed the advice of other reviewers and dredged the chicken in flour first. Then I sauteed an onion and some peppers and set aside. Next was to quickly sear/brown bite-sized pieces of chicken (you want that crunchy coating) and added the sauce and cooked veggies to simmer. For the hot sauce you MUST use Sriracha Hot Chili Sauce (Rooster Sauce). It MAKES the dish. My chicken was sticky, sweet and spicy just the way it was supposed to be. What an amazing flavor profile. I'm thrilled with this recipe!

AWESOME AWESOME chicken. Used ground ginger and 1 tbs. of hot sauce but could hardly taste it. If you like spicey, use both. My came out VERY sticky! Here's what I did: cut up chicken into small chuncks, put in bag with flour and shake until lightly coated. Put in frying pan at #8 of 10...very hot, until started to really brown. Took several minutes. Then I added the sauce, tossed, dropped to #3 and put lid on until rice was done, probably 15 minutes. Continue to use the same pan even though the chicken sticks and burns on the botton!!!! All that stuff makes it sticky! Will make again and again!
Followed other suggestions of cornstarch coaling on the chicken first. Cooked the chicken in two batches and added 2 heads of broccoli to the second batch. doubled the sauce and it turned out perfect

Yum! This was delicious but I made a few changes based on comments and to make this a little more healthy as well. The first thing I did was heat a bag of stir fry veggies in a wok, then I set aside. I doubled the sauce and used a brown sugar-free substitute, and coconut aminos instead of soy sauce. I also used 1/2 the hot sauce as I wasn't sure that would fly with my kids. I let this cook separately in a pan. I sliced up 2 lbs of boneless, skinless chicken thighs, lightly seasoned and rolled in corn starch prior to cooking in a wok. Once the chicken was finished cooking (in batches) I added the veggies and sauce in and served over cauliflower rice. Everyone cleaned their plates.

Both my husband and I thought this was excellent. I followed suggestions from other reviews and lightly floured the chicken and added a tsp of corn starch to the sauce. It thickened up nicely and had great flavor. Will definitely make again. Thanks Kate for posting
I love this recipe! I added two tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with water to help thicken the sauce, and it worked perfectly. We also topped it with some roasted peanuts for extra flavor and crunch.
I used half the soy sauce as suggested by another reviewer. I also used corn starch to thicken the sauce as suggested. Delicious!

Amazing!!!! My whole family just loved this dinner!! I doubled the sauce, sauteed 3 bell peppers, onion and garlic in olive oil and set it aside. Tossed the chicken with flour, salt and pepper, sautéed it in the same pan I used for the veggies on high heat and scraped the pan as i went along, I then added the sauce, cooked it for a few minutes scrapping all the yummy pieces off the bottom of the pan, added the veggies and cooked till sauce was thickened. Served it over brown rice and devoured it!!!
I covered my chicken and flour before I fried it for a little extra crunchy. This also helped the sauce thicken and I added broccoli for some green. It was wonderful.
Excellent. Followed the dredging chicken in flour and added a bag of stir fry veg.
Off the chart. Delicious. I cleaned my plate. I never do. I made crisp steamed asparagus alongside small side of white cilantro rice. Absolutely delicious!.

I made this dish last night and it was delicious. I followed the advice in some of the reviews and put chicken in a flour/cornstarch mix. Worked beautifully. Next time I make it I will add the broccoli for a veggie component.
First time making it, followed instructions written, used Sriracha for hot sauce, most excellent! Wife loved it.
I made this recipe using suggestions by others to dredge the chicken in order to thicken the sauce. I think that was a good move. The flavors were okay but nothing special.
It just was not a dish I enjoyed.
I enjoyed the spicy and sweet test of this dish. One review suggested dredging the chicken in flour first and it worked well to thicken the sauce.
So good

The whole house loved this! I dredged the chicken bits through a combination of cornstarch and flour with some salt and pepper like others did. Perfectly crispy but tender too. Will definitely make again
